articles.title: European football: Lazio beat Parma to top Serie A; Dortmund lead Bundesliga
articles.summary: Lazio win 2-1 while Roma draw 3-3 with Napoli. Beier gives Dortmund win over Eintracht Frankfurt. Lazio climbed to the top of Serie A with a 2-1 home win ⁠over Parma ⁠as Roma ​twice came from behind to secure a 3-3 draw with Napoli in a pulsating clash in Naples.
body: Lazio have 22 points from their eight matches this ⁠season and are three points clear of champions Inter Milan, who have played a game fewer and host Fiorentina on Sunday. Lazio opened the scoring in the 50th minute as Kenneth Taylor ⁠struck his first of the season, before Parma’s Diego Carlos put the ball into his own net trying ​to cut out a cross. The visitors scored a ‌late consolation through Simone Lontani.

Third-placed Roma ‌trailed 2-0 and then 3-2 late on, so will be pleased with a point in Naples as they preserved ‌their 15-game unbeaten league run that dates back to April. Frank Anguissa’s spectacular overhead kick gave Napoli the lead and Scott McTominay doubled the advantage.

At that stage they were cruising, but two goals in four minutes from Matías Soulé and Leonardo Balerdi drew Roma level. When McTominay added his second in the closing stages the momentum swung back in Napoli’s favour, but Balerdi headed an equaliser for Roma with a minute remaining.

articles.title: Smith retains title with split-decision win over Puello
articles.summary: Britain's Dalton Smith defends his WBC light-welterweight world title with a split-decision victory over Alberto Puello in a triumphant homecoming in Sheffield.
body: The 29-year-old extended his unbeaten professional record in a high-class tactical contest at the Utilita Arena, with both fighters displaying sharp counter-punching skills.
The result hung in the balance as the judges' scorecards were read out, with victory for either man or a draw seemingly possible.
But Smith edged it, with two judges scoring the contest 115-113 in his favour and the third awarding it 116-112 to Dominican fighter Puello.
It was Smith's first title defence after his stunning fifth-round knockout of Subriel Matias in Brooklyn in January.

articles.title: Nashville SC seal first MLS Supporters’ Shield with 2-0 win over CF Montreal
articles.summary: Surridge and Mukhtar fire Nashville to 2-0 victory. Nashville extend unbeaten streak to seven matches. Montreal teenager Keita impresses on MLS debut. Nashville SC scored twice in the second half to claim the Supporters’ Shield as the top team in MLS with a 2-0 win at CF Montreal on Saturday.
body: The win allowed Nashville (21-3-7, 70 points) to stretch their unbeaten streak to seven games (5-0-2).
Montreal (6-18-7, 25 points) have just one win in their past 11 games (1-8-2) and have been officially eliminated from playoff contention.

Sam Surridge buried his own rebound to give Nashville a 1-0 lead in the 52nd minute. Montreal goalkeeper Samsy Keita, the 17-year-old homegrown player making his MLS debut, denied Surridge’s header from the right side of the goal area off a cross from Reed Baker-Whiting. The rebound went right to Surridge, who easily put it into the far side for his team-leading 18th goal of the season.

Hany Mukhtar made it 2-0 in the 76th minute. He intercepted defender Brayan Vera’s clearing attempt outside the box, was first to it as it rolled inside the box and then hit a shot that deflected off Keita and into the net from the top right corner of the goal area.

articles.title: Alonso urges Cole Palmer ‘to learn’ from red card in Chelsea’s defeat to Spurs
articles.summary: Forward sent off after 80 minutes for second yellow card. ‘We need to have maturity to deal with difficult moments’ Xabi Alonso said that Cole Palmer must learn from his red card during Chelsea’s shock 2-0 defeat to Tottenham, who claimed their first win at Stamford Bridge since 2018 thanks to an…
body: Spurs, who had won on one of their previous 34 trips to west London, were already 1-0 up when Palmer earned a second yellow card for catching Conor Gallagher with a late tackle. The playmaker could have been sent off earlier – his first booking came during a clash with Mateus Fernandes – and Alonso agreed that this could be an important lesson for the 24-year-old.

“Absolutely,” Chelsea’s manager said. “I haven’t seen them [back] on TV but as far as I have been told probably he [the referee] got it right. We need to have this maturity to deal with difficult moments. When you have conceded for 1-0, still probably it was 15-20 minutes to go. I need to check the action to talk with Cole but it is one to learn for the future for sure.”

Alonso said there are no wider concerns with Palmer’s character, even though Chelsea’s No 10 could have been sent off against Everton last weekend too. “Today, for sure, yes, but it is not a concern,” Alonso said. “It is a moment to keep calm, a moment to keep mature, for everyone.”

articles.title: Man Utd not an unmanageable club - Carrick
articles.summary: Michael Carrick says it is possible to manage Manchester United effectively as he clings on to his job with Bournemouth visiting Old Trafford on Sunday.
body: Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick has dismissed a theory the Old Trafford club are unmanageable.
Carrick is clinging on to his job after a desperate run of seven games without a win before Sunday's Premier League home game against Bournemouth (14:00 GMT).
The pressure on him has been heightened by controversial comments from senior players Lisandro Martinez and Bruno Fernandes attacking the club's recruitment and his tactics.

If Carrick were to lose his job, it would be the third change of manager in as many seasons and mean eight long-term bosses, including Ralf Rangnick, have lost their jobs after failing to get close to the heights of Sir Alex Ferguson, who retired in 2013.

articles.title: The candid meeting that 'changed' Spurs - are they finally on way back?
articles.summary: Tottenham end Saturday's Premier League action in 12th place, their highest league position since 2 January. Are they finally on their way back?
body: Whisper it quietly, but could Spurs finally be on their way back?
Tottenham's 2-0 win at Chelsea on Saturday moved them up to the heady heights of 12th in the Premier League - their highest league position since 2 January.
And, after back-to-back 17th-placed finishes, there are growing signs Roberto de Zerbi's side are showing there is real light at the end of a pretty dark tunnel.
Saturday's impressive win at Stamford Bridge was just the second time they have won two league games in a row in 42 attempts - inspired by starring roles from James Maddison and Mathys Tel.

articles.summary: The agent of Barcelona star Alejandro Balde is scouring the market for a potential new landing spot for his client following the turn of the year. Full-back Balde is for his part in the midst of what has been a hugely challenging opening to the new campaign in Catalunya’s capital.
body: Sitting behind both Xavi Espart and João Cancelo in the pecking order on the left of boss Hansi Flick’s backline, the Spaniard has been restricted to just a pair of appearances in all competitions.
Balde was linked with a departure from the Camp Nou over the summer, but ultimately made the call to stay put to fight for his place.
As alluded to above, though, if the latest word stemming from the media this week is anything to go by, then the 22-year-old staying put through January appears far from certain.

‘His agent, Jorge Mendes, is exploring different alternatives to find a way out for the player. Mendes would have offered Balde to Roma, who are studying the possibility of signing him during the January transfer window.’

articles.title: Rice's late comeback falls short as Owls suffer 7th straight loss in shootout vs. Florida Atlantic
articles.summary: BOCA RATON, Fla. - A new starting quarterback provided a spark. But it wasn't enough for Rice to end its losing streak. Rice dropped its seventh straight game Saturday, falling 51-49 to Florida Atlantic in a shootout between Owls squads at Flagler Credit Union Stadium.
body: Rice (1-7, 0-4 American) saw its defeat sealed with 45 seconds left, when Tommy Bauchiero's 55-yard field goal attempt fell short, allowing FAU (5-2, 2-1) to escape with the win.
Gael Ochoa drew his first start at QB for Rice, and ran for 259 yards on 12 carries, scoring four touchdowns as his team rolled up 608 total yards.

Ochoa ran for 55- and 52-yard touchdowns as Rice took an early 14-0 lead before giving up the next 23 points. Rice trailed 23-21 at halftime, with the difference being a safety on a blocked put by Derrick Rogers Jr.
Rice stayed within striking distance in the second half, but Easton Messer's fifth TD of the game - an 82-yard punt return - gave FAU a nine-point lead with 3:37 left in the fourth quarter.

The setback comes at an inconvenient time for Bayern Munich, who are preparing for a difficult away fixture amid an already challenging week fo llowing Vincent Kompany’s health scare.

Neuer’s absence means Jonas Urbig is likely to take over between the posts. The young goalkeeper has been viewed as Neuer’s long-term successor, and another opportunity to demonstrate his readiness would be a signifi cant moment in his development.

However, Bayern Munich will need more than a confident performance from their goalkeeper to navigate a tricky encounter against SC Freiburg. The hosts are a dangerous opponent, and Bayern Munich cannot afford to let the uncertainty surrounding the squad’s availability become a distraction.
With Kompany recovering, Joshua Kimmich still away from the team for family reasons, and Kim Min-jae also unavaila ble, Bayern Munich have already lost several important figures for this weekend.

articles.title: Littler powers past Aspinall to reach European Championship quarter-finals
articles.summary: Luke Littler remains on course to win the one major title he's never won as he beat Nathan Aspinall 10-5 in the second round of the European Championship Darts on Saturday evening.
body: Littler produced the second-best average in the competition's history - his 114.47 has only ever been bettered by Phil Taylor's 118.14 - as he secured an impressive victory in Dortmund.

Aspinall produced ten 180s in the match - three more than his opponent - but it wasn't enough to survive the onslaught from the world No 1, who won the first four legs of the match in 12 darts or fewer.

Aspinall briefly rallied to reduce the score to 5-4, but Littler controlled the second half of the game and, despite one brief interruption to deal with a vocal fan in the crowd, he ultimately closed out the match on D10.
"I knew the start was good. I was gutted at giving him a leg and going into the first break at 4-1 when I wanted 5-0.

articles.title: Forget Sean O’Malley! Song Yadong gets the No. 1 contender rub at UFC 333
articles.summary: Sean O’Malley seemed pretty convinced that a Petr Yan win at UFC 333 would result in a “Suga” title shot. But we’re not so sure any more after seeing the UFC push Song Yadong on the Abu Dhabi broadcast.
body: O’Malley holds a controversial split decision win over Yan from 2022, so there’s a baked in storyline to hype up a potential rematch for Yan’s bantamweight belt. Yan started slow in Abu Dhabi against Merab Dvalishvili but turned up the heat in round three to win the fight convincingly, 48-47 on all three judges score cards (highlights here).

After an uncertain start, O’Malley must have thought that was sweet. But things got a bit sour after Yan was announced the winner and color commentator Daniel Cormier suggested Song Yadong, who was in attendance in Abu Dhabi, was the real No. 1 contender. O’Malley? Unmentioned.
Yan seemed uninterested in winning back that loss against O’Malley, too. Instead, he suggested Sean was a bit too used to getting gift title shots.

articles.title: Alonso 'out-coached', 'petulant' Palmer and Penders howler: Chelsea's horror night
articles.summary: They say bad things come in threes. That was certainly the case for Chelsea on a miserable evening at Stamford Bridge as they lost 2-0 to Tottenham and were described as "awful" by Gary Neville.
body: Spurs had won only one of their previous 34 Premier League visits to Chelsea but dominated Xabi Alonso's side from start to finish, with an own goal from Mike Penders and a stunning late strike from Mathys Tel securing a well-deserved win for Roberto De Zerbi's side.

To add to their woes, on an evening where the dismal weather matched their performance, Cole Palmer was sent off for a second bookable offence after already escaping a straight red card earlier in the game, having barged into Spurs midfielder Mateus Fernandes.

"Tottenham outplayed Chelsea. Out-coached, everything. None of us expected Tottenham to come here and win today, but after 10-15 mins, that confidence did start to grow," said Neville while on commentary, in a game that was also described as the worst performance of Alonso's short tenure so far.
"Chelsea have been awful, really. On the ball, they've been well short. Nowhere near the level. I am stunned."
